questions.q: What did the Earthrise photograph help set off, according to the summary?
a: A wave of environmental legislation and public concern
A new era of military spending in space
A decline in funding for scientific research
A movement to colonize the moon
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the image led to laws on pesticides and emissions, plus Earth Day and clean air and water acts.

questions.q: Why does Tyson argue that exploration is necessary?
a: It is how humanity keeps pace with exponential change
It guarantees economic growth for every nation
It proves that other planets can support life
It replaces the need for scientific education
questions.why: Lesson 2 says that without pushing what we know and can build, nature will eventually overwhelm us.

questions.q: What example shows how exponential progress helped during the pandemic?
a: Instant global communication, mass-produced equipment and fast vaccines
The rapid decline of international air travel
A worldwide shift to remote schooling
Better understanding of compound interest
questions.why: Lesson 2 asks how many more would have died without those tools, which exponential science made possible.

questions.q: What did Tyson notice about the library shelves at Princeton?
a: The total amount of research doubled roughly every 15 years
Most journals had stopped publishing new papers
Older papers were far more cited than recent ones
Half the shelves held research from before 1900
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses this observation to show that human knowledge itself grows exponentially.

questions.q: What does the enormous number 10 to the power of 30 represent?
a: All the genetically possible people who could ever be born
The number of stars in the observable universe
The age of the universe in years
The number of people alive on Earth today
questions.why: Lesson 3 says that is the total of genetically possible humans, of which only a tiny fraction has existed.
